clue.text: Composition of nine songs changing key

indicators.note: changing tells us the letters of nine songs are to be rearranged

parts.note: E is one of the musical keys, named by its letter

explanation.surface: A medley of nine songs that shifts from one key to another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges NINESONGS; the key E is added at the end. Satie, the puzzle's theme, wrote a set of these piano pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Satie coined this title for a set of his piano pieces, so it names a musical work.

clue.text: Standard alpha female

parts.note: a norm is a standard or benchmark
alpha is the NATO phonetic word for the letter A

explanation.surface: A description of a typical dominant woman: the standard alpha female.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alpha female' reads as one phrase, but alpha just gives A and 'female' is the definition, a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a woman's given name, as in Bellini's opera heroine, so it can stand for a female.

clue.text: Boxer in book about African country

indicators.note: in places the boxer inside the reversed book
about tells us the book's name is turned round

parts.note: Amos is a book of the Old Testament
Muhammad Ali, the famous heavyweight boxer

explanation.surface: A boxer appears in a book about an African country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxer' here is the champion Muhammad Ali, and 'about' turns the Old Testament book round to give SOMA, which 'in' then opens up.
explanation.definitionFit: The Horn of Africa nation with Mogadishu as its capital.

clue.text: Extra small picture of some poinsettias

indicators.note: some of says only part of the word poinsettias is wanted

explanation.surface: An additional little picture showing a few poinsettias.
explanation.definitionFit: A small picture set within a larger one, as on a map, is an extra small image.

clue.text: Horse has eaten nothing — surely eyes bulge initially, seeing this?

definitions.text: Horse has eaten nothing — surely eyes bulge initially, seeing this?

indicators.note: has eaten means the horse word swallows the other letters

parts.note: a nag is an old horse
nothing is zero, the letter O

indicators.note: initially takes the first letters of surely, eyes and bulge

explanation.surface: A starving horse goggles at the sight of its feed bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has eaten' and 'initially' do the work, yet read whole the clue also pictures what a hungry horse would goggle at, so it doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bag of feed hung over a horse's head is exactly what a starving horse would goggle at.

clue.text: Barman taking up current job in the Republic of Ireland

indicators.note: in a down clue, taking up means reading upward, so the whole is reversed
in places current and job inside the country's name

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name of the Republic of Ireland
I is the symbol for electric current
a task is a job

explanation.surface: A bartender takes up a new post in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' builds EITASKIRE, which 'taking up' reverses. 'Barman' is not a bartender: it means a man of musical bars, a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: A composer writes music in bars, so the cryptic sense of barman is a composer such as Satie.

clue.text: Go plum over fences

indicators.note: fences means the two words enclose the letters wanted, which run across the gap between them

explanation.surface: A horse called Plum is urged to go over the fences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plum' and 'over' look like horse racing, but 'fences' means they hold the answer between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a turn in a game, as in chess, is having a go.

clue.text: Me, a stripper? Not half — with a little jiggle for the best barmen!

indicators.note: a jiggle shakes these letters into a new order
not half keeps only the first half of the word stripper

explanation.surface: A cheeky stripper boasting about her routine, jiggling for the best bartenders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' gives STRI from stripper; 'with a little jiggle' rearranges ME A STRI. Barmen are composers, men of musical bars.
explanation.definitionFit: Masters of music, especially great conductors and composers, are the finest writers of musical bars.

clue.text: Sex? No ta, I've endless "nasty headaches"

indicators.note: nasty signals that the letters are mangled into a new order
endless drops the last letter of the word I've

explanation.surface: A partner refuses sex, pleading a string of awful headaches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts I've to IV; 'nasty' rearranges SEXNOTAIV. It is also the title of Satie's piece meant to be played 840 times.
explanation.definitionFit: Annoyances and irritations are figurative headaches.

clue.text: 23D gets negligent, going round European building site

parts.note: the answer to 23 down is a musical instrument, whose name abbreviates to P in musical notation for soft

indicators.note: going round means the negligent word encloses European

parts.note: remiss means careless or negligent

explanation.surface: A careless instrument is somehow placed around a European building site.
explanation.walkthrough: P stands for piano (softly) in music, so 23 down supplies P.
explanation.definitionFit: A building with its land, as in business property, is a site with buildings.

clue.text: Climber's aid caught by current after originally falling in river

indicators.note: by places caught beside current

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: falling in means dropping into the river's name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon

indicators.note: originally takes the first letter of the word after

explanation.surface: A climbing tool is swept away after falling into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' sets C beside I; 'originally' takes A from 'after', and 'falling in' drops it into EXE, the Devon river. The surface wants 'caught by current' to be a drowning.
explanation.definitionFit: Mountaineers use this pick-like tool to cut steps and steady themselves on ice.

clue.text: Inform sailor about dance 23A?

indicators.note: about tells us the joined words are turned round

parts.note: to tell is to inform
AB, able seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: Tell the sailor about the dance parade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses TELL + AB. Parade (23 across) was a Satie ballet, so the definition names the kind of work it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Satie's Parade was a staged dance work for Diaghilev, an example of this art form.

clue.text: Those flying over USA, encrypted thus within digital data

indicators.note: within means the scrambled word goes inside the data

parts.note: bits are the units of digital data

indicators.note: encrypted signals the word thus is scrambled

explanation.surface: Something about spy planes over America whose signals are encrypted in digital data.
explanation.walkthrough: 'encrypted' makes USHT and 'within' places it. 'Those flying over USA' sounds like aircraft but means American songbirds.
explanation.definitionFit: These small long-tailed songbirds of western North America fly over the United States.

clue.text: College lost broadcast by English comedian

parts.note: L stands for lost in sports results tables
to air is to broadcast

explanation.surface: A college has lost a programme aired by an English comic.
explanation.walkthrough: Jenny Éclair is a British stand-up comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: Jenny Éclair is a well-known British stand-up comic, a Perrier Award winner.

clue.text: Taxi to go across the Pyrenees, at first only for Spanish gent

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
aller is the French verb 'to go', the language across the Pyrenees from Spain

indicators.note: at first takes the first letter of only

explanation.surface: Taking a taxi across the Pyrenees for a Spanish gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: In Spanish the word means a gentleman or knight, a Spanish gent.

clue.text: A house in Germany ordered the cigars

indicators.note: ordered signals the letters of the cigars are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A German household places an order for cigars.
explanation.definitionFit: The building in Berlin where the German parliament sits, a legislative house.

clue.text: Eliminate misuse of "Frog" with edit

indicators.note: misuse of means the words are mangled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Remove a mistaken use of the word Frog by editing.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispose of something completely is to eliminate it.

clue.text: Backing musical about Sting, in vain

indicators.note: backing means the whole is read backwards
about means the musical goes round the sting word

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical
to sting someone is to rob or swindle them

explanation.surface: Supporting a musical about the singer Sting proved fruitless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' gives EVITROBA, which 'Backing' reverses. Sting looks like the singer but means swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: An attempt that fails to achieve its aim is fruitless, done to no purpose.

clue.text: Film with female actor as cowboy?

parts.note: Ran is Kurosawa's 1985 film
Cher is a singer and Oscar-winning actress

explanation.surface: A film in which a female star plays a cowboy.
explanation.definitionFit: A cattle farmer in the American West is loosely a cowboy, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Mistake made by traitor beset by hesitancies

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by the hesitancies

parts.note: er and um are two hesitant noises
a rat is a traitor

explanation.surface: A traitor, stammering with ums and ers, makes a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A printing error listed for correction is a mistake.

clue.text: After falling asleep, pass away

indicators.note: falling signals the letters of asleep tumble into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone dies peacefully after falling asleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pass away' looks like dying, but it means time going by.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that slips by is said to go by or pass, as in weeks going past.

clue.text: A game that's cut short

parts.note: bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A game that was ended early.
explanation.definitionFit: To shorten a text is to condense it, cutting it short.

clue.text: Decisive argument sees king escape jail in France, dear

indicators.note: escape means the king letter gets out of the jail word

parts.note: clink is slang for jail
K is the chess abbreviation for king
cher is French for dear

explanation.surface: A king breaking out of a French jail settles the argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A point that settles a debate conclusively is a decisive argument.

clue.text: Show a diaper needs changing after letting one go

indicators.note: needs changing signals that the remaining letters are rearranged
letting one go means the one is released from the word diaper

parts.note: I is the roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A soiled nappy, after someone lets one go, needs changing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letting ... go' removes I (one) from A DIAPER, and 'needs changing' rearranges ADAPER. Satie wrote a ballet of this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A procession or display is a show, as in a parade of troops.

clue.text: Architect coming up from Verona, I presume

indicators.note: coming up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A greeting to an architect arriving from Verona, in the manner of Stanley meeting Livingstone.
explanation.definitionFit: Renzo Piano is the Italian architect behind the Shard and the Pompidou Centre.

clue.text: Girl hiding stolen garment

indicators.note: hiding means the girl's name wraps around the stolen word

parts.note: Di is a girl's name
hot is slang for stolen

explanation.surface: A girl concealing a stolen item of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A loincloth worn by Hindu men in India is an item of clothing.

clue.text: The Clarion rent Paris venue? C'est bonne chance, peut-être

definitions.text: Paris venue? C'est bonne chance, peut-être

indicators.note: rent means torn apart, so the letters of The Clarion are rearranged

explanation.surface: A newspaper's tear-off item about a Parisian place, with a French aside about good luck.
explanation.walkthrough: The French tag says 'it's good luck, perhaps': a black cat brings luck. Satie played piano at this Montmartre cabaret.
explanation.definitionFit: This Montmartre cabaret, named after a lucky black cat, was a Paris nightspot where Satie played piano.

clue.text: One might show a little joy, if rent to fall

definitions.text: One might show a little joy

parts.note: a rent is a tear or rip
to drop is to fall

explanation.surface: Someone's joy shows a little, though a rip lets it slip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like payment but is a rip.
explanation.definitionFit: People weep from happiness, so a single bead of crying can reveal a little joy.

clue.text: See 25
Work that's needed to turn up one's toes after PE? On the contrary!

indicators.note: after places the dying word last

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school gym
nope is a slangy no, a flat contradiction
to turn up one's toes is to die

explanation.surface: A wry line about PE classes being enough to kill you.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface misleads: 'PE' gives GYM, and 'On the contrary!' gives NOPE, not a reversal. A famous Satie piano piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Satie's best-known piano pieces carry this title, so it names a musical work.
